subject.mainFocus: Expanding Inventory 3.0 into a complete product-information system while repairing internal routing and establishing a stable Apps Script deployment method.
subject.description: Klinswork work update for July 23, 2026, covering Inventory 3.0 product pages, routing repairs, stable Apps Script deployment links, filtering improvements, product research, and deployment safeguards.

narrative.promptingSituation: Inventory 3.0 had a working inventory browser, but product information remained limited to compact details, products without balances were harder to reach, and internal routing could lead from the correct app into a blank or older-looking page.
narrative.initialUnderstanding: The visible failure looked like a changing deployment URL, while the broader product experience needed full pages, better filtering, and stronger safety-information access.
narrative.intendedOutcome: Create complete standalone product pages, improve inventory browsing, document new products, repair all internal navigation, and preserve one stable deployment address.
narrative.approach: Add direct product routes, retain the quick details popup, refine filtering, document the liner products, trace routing to the exact client-side helper, replace temporary runtime-derived URLs with the server-provided APP_URL, and define a safer deployment workflow.

progression.description: Added direct product routes and full product-information views with SDS access and return navigation.
progression.result: Inventory 3.0 gained standalone product pages while retaining quick details.

progression.result: Daily browsing became less cluttered while the full active catalog remained accessible.

progression.title: Diagnosed the routing failure
progression.description: Traced incorrect links to getAppBaseUrl() rebuilding routes from window.location inside the Apps Script iframe.
progression.result: The apparent deployment problem was reclassified as an internal base-URL problem.

progression.title: Established stable routing and deployment rules
progression.description: Changed internal routing to use window.APP_URL provided by ScriptApp.getService().getUrl().
progression.result: Product and return links worked without changing the public deployment URL.

problemsEncountered.problem: Full product-page links could open a blank or older-looking page.
problemsEncountered.effect: Users appeared to leave the correct deployment even though the public /exec URL had not changed.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Rewrote getAppBaseUrl() to use the server-provided window.APP_URL.

problemsEncountered.problem: The deployment workflow was being confused with ordinary deployment-version updates.
problemsEncountered.effect: New deployments could produce unnecessary new URLs and leave older versions active.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Established the rule to update an existing deployment with a new version for normal code changes.

unsuccessfulApproaches.approach: Build internal links from window.location.origin and window.location.pathname.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItWasTried: It appeared to provide the current application's base address.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItDidNotWork: Inside Apps Script it resolved to a temporary googleusercontent iframe address rather than the canonical /exec URL.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whatWasLearned: Internal routes must use the server-provided canonical deployment URL.

unsuccessfulApproaches.approach: Treat the routing failure as evidence that the deployment URL had changed.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItWasTried: The destination looked like a different or stale application version.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItDidNotWork: The outside deployment remained stable; only client-generated internal links were wrong.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whatWasLearned: Separate public deployment identity from temporary runtime iframe location.

turningPoints.title: The deployment URL was proven stable
turningPoints.description: The investigation showed that the external /exec address was not changing.
turningPoints.effectOnDirection: Debugging shifted from deployment management to client-side routing.

turningPoints.title: window.APP_URL became the canonical source
turningPoints.description: The app was already receiving the correct URL from ScriptApp.getService().getUrl().
turningPoints.effectOnDirection: One base URL could now drive every internal route.

keyDecisions.decision: Retain the compact Details popup while adding full product pages.
keyDecisions.reason: Quick reference and complete product information serve different usage needs.
alternativesConsidered: Replace the popup entirely with full-page navigation
consequences: Users can choose quick inspection or detailed product review.

keyDecisions.decision: Make In stock only the default browser view.
keyDecisions.reason: Routine inventory work should remain focused on products actually present at the selected location.
alternativesConsidered: Show the full active catalog by default
consequences: Daily clutter is reduced while All products remains available for new opening balances.

keyDecisions.decision: Use one canonical server-provided base URL for all routes.
keyDecisions.reason: Runtime iframe addresses are temporary and unsuitable for stable navigation.
consequences: Internal links remain stable across ordinary deployment-version updates.

narrative.methodEstablished: For Apps Script applications, obtain the canonical /exec URL on the server, expose it to the browser as window.APP_URL, and build every internal route from that single source.
narrative.result: Inventory 3.0 became a more complete product, inventory, and safety-information system with stable product routing and a clearer deployment process.
lessonsLearned: A temporary Apps Script iframe URL must never be treated as the application's canonical base.
Ordinary code updates should create a new deployment version, not a new deployment.
Product browsing can serve both daily inventory and catalog-management needs through separate default and full views.
Manufactured articles such as trash liners belong in product inventory rather than the SDS directory.
narrative.directionChange: The project moved from a quantity-focused inventory browser toward a richer product-information and safety-reference system.
narrative.narrativeSummary: The July 23 work expanded product capabilities, improved filtering, documented new supplies, and resolved a misleading Apps Script routing problem by separating stable deployment identity from temporary runtime location.

projectSpecificLessons: Full product pages and compact details can coexist because they serve different operational needs.
Inventory filtering should default to the most common daily-use view while preserving catalog access.
generalLessons: Temporary iframe URLs are runtime implementation details, not application identities.
Ordinary Apps Script code updates should preserve the deployment ID and /exec URL.

knowledgeBaseCandidates.title: Stable internal routing in Apps Script
knowledgeBaseCandidates.description: Use ScriptApp.getService().getUrl() on the server, expose it to the browser, and build all internal links from that value.

knowledgeBaseCandidates.title: Apps Script deployment versus deployment version

rulesConfirmedOrRevised.rule: Do not use window.location or document.location as the canonical base for Apps Script routing.
rulesConfirmedOrRevised.explanation: Those values can point to temporary googleusercontent runtime addresses.

rulesConfirmedOrRevised.rule: Do not create a new deployment for ordinary code changes.
rulesConfirmedOrRevised.explanation: Updating the existing deployment with a new version preserves bookmarks, Google Sites buttons, and QR codes.

sections.title: Full product pages
sections.contentSummary: Direct product routes were established with a product identifier in the web-app address. The application can now open directly to a specific product while preserving access to the main inventory screen. Information shown on each page Product image and category Product name and manufacturer Manufacturer product code Container size and inventory unit Inventory product ID SDS revision, source, and verification information Direct SDS and manufacturer-information buttons when available Navigation and presentation The original Details popup was retained for quick reference. An Open full product page button was added. Back-to-Inventory links were provided at both the top and bottom. Broken images now fall back to a clean placeholder. Temporary route-testing alerts and debug material were removed. The final detail page was tested and confirmed to look excellent.

sections.title: Apps Script routing failure diagnosed and repaired
sections.contentSummary: Inventory 3.0 could open correctly from Google Sites, but the Open full product page button could then lead to a blank or older-looking page. The failure appeared to be a deployment problem, but the actual cause was inside Scripts.html . Incorrect routing source Inside an Apps Script application, this can resolve to a temporary address containing: Correct routing source The application was already receiving the stable deployment address from Apps Script: The getAppBaseUrl() helper was rewritten to use window.APP_URL . This repaired the full-product-page link and both Back-to-Inventory links without changing the outside deployment URL.

sections.title: Stable deployment workflow established
sections.contentSummary: The difference between an Apps Script deployment and a deployment version was clarified. Existing deployment Edit through Manage deployments . Select New version . Keep the same deployment ID and /exec URL. Preserve bookmarks, Google Sites buttons, and QR codes. New deployment Creates another deployment ID. Produces another /exec URL. Can leave older versions active and accessible. Should not be used for ordinary code updates. Protected navigation rules Do not build internal app links from window.location . Do not use document.location for application routing. Do not store temporary googleusercontent.com addresses. Do not hard-code deployment URLs inside client-side scripts. Use the server-provided window.APP_URL consistently. Short post-deployment test Open the Inventory 3.0 homepage. Select a location. Open a product’s Details panel. Open the full product page. Test Back to Inventory.

sections.title: Longer-term application architecture
sections.contentSummary: A central Klinswork URL registry was considered as a way to manage the addresses of Inventory 3.0, Tasker, Email Composer, and the Tool Center. Such a registry may still be useful for internal navigation and future replacement deployments. The more important discovery, however, is that normal code updates should not require any link changes at all. Stable deployment URLs combined with a single canonical internal base URL remove most of the need for manual link maintenance.

sections.title: The larger achievement
sections.contentSummary: Today’s work substantially expanded Inventory 3.0 while also resolving one of the most confusing problems in Apps Script development: apparently changing links that were actually temporary runtime addresses. A complete product-information page system was established. Product filtering became more practical for daily inventory work. SDS access was integrated into product pages. Two trash-liner products were documented for the catalog. The full-page routing failure was traced to its exact function. The entire corrected Scripts.html file was produced and deployed. The stable deployment URL was preserved and verified. The final product detail page was confirmed to work and look excellent. By the end of the session, Inventory 3.0 was no longer only a quantity tracker. It had become a more complete product, inventory, and safety information system with dependable routing and a clearer…
